tagline: Istanbul's design and coffee district — Karaköy blends Ottoman port history with galleries, baklavas, and the city's best specialty coffee scene.

items.name: Kronotrop
items.description: One of Turkey's original specialty coffee pioneers. The Karaköy branch is a benchmark — excellent espresso, careful sourcing, great atmosphere.

items.name: Petra Roasting Co.
items.description: A favourite among Istanbul's coffee community. Small space, serious roasting operation, and consistently excellent cups.
items.tip: The filter coffee changes regularly based on what they've just roasted. Always worth asking.

items.name: Karaköy Güllüoğlu
items.description: Not a café — but a morning cup of Turkish tea with fresh baklava at this legendary shop is an Istanbul ritual you shouldn't miss.
items.tip: Go in the morning when the baklava is fresh. The fıstıklı (pistachio) is the classic choice.

items.name: Karaköy Lokantası
items.description: Modern Turkish cuisine done with precision. Seasonal menus, beautiful presentation, and a calm atmosphere for a proper lunch.

items.name: Karaköy Güllüoğlu
items.description: The original and best baklava shop in Istanbul — possibly the world. Fresh baklava made daily with Antep pistachios.
items.tip: Order by weight at the counter. A 200g assorted box makes a perfect gift.

items.name: Tarihi Karaköy Balık Ekmek
items.description: A simple stall near the docks serving the city's best balık ekmek (fish sandwich). Fresh mackerel, onion, parsley, bread.
items.tip: Best at lunchtime when the fish is freshest. ₺60-80 and worth every lira.

items.name: Şehzade Cağ Kebabı
items.description: Horizontal rotisserie kebab from Erzurum — a completely different style from the standard döner. Exceptional quality.
items.tip: Order the full portion with lavash bread. It's filling — one portion is enough for most people.

items.name: Vault Karaköy
items.description: Rooftop bar in a converted bank vault. Excellent cocktails, great views of the Golden Horn and Galata Tower at night.
items.tip: Book ahead for the rooftop — it fills fast in the evenings.

items.name: Karaköy Rooms Bar
items.description: A boutique hotel bar with an excellent cocktail programme and a cool, design-forward atmosphere. Good for a quiet drink.

items.name: Unter
items.description: A Karaköy favourite — a small, atmospheric bar known for its cocktails and vinyl collection. Very local crowd.

items.name: Istanbul Modern
items.description: Turkey's leading contemporary art museum, recently reopened in a stunning new waterfront building. World-class collection and great temporary exhibitions.
items.tip: Free on Thursdays. The restaurant inside has one of the best views in Istanbul.

items.name: Galata Tower
items.description: The 9th-century tower that defines Istanbul's skyline. The view from the top is excellent — especially at dusk. A short uphill walk from Karaköy.
items.tip: Buy tickets online to skip the queue. Go at sunset for the best light.

items.name: Karaköy Design Shops
items.description: Karaköy has a cluster of excellent independent design, homeware, and clothing shops along Kemankeş Caddesi and its side streets.

items.name: Galata Bridge Walk
items.description: Walk across Galata Bridge from Karaköy to Eminönü for ferry views, fishermen, and one of the great urban crossings in the world.

tips: Karaköy is tiny and very walkable. Most of the best spots are within a 5-minute walk of each other on Kemankeş Caddesi.
The ferry to Kadiköy leaves from Karaköy İskelesi — a 20-minute, ₺15 crossing that's far better than driving.
Karaköy gets extremely busy on weekends. Weekday mornings are the sweet spot for exploring the coffee and design scene.
The uphill walk from Karaköy to Galata Tower takes 10 minutes but there's a funicular (tünel) if your legs aren't up for it.
